skill.name: impress
skill.description: Create, edit, automate, and convert LibreOffice Impress presentations across ODP, PPTX, and PDF workflows.
skill.summary: Automate LibreOffice Impress creation, templating, conversion, and batch processing.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are scanner artifacts from Markdown fences, local conversion commands, temporary directory use, and official documentation links. One static finding is confirmed because the troubleshooting command opens an unauthenticated localhost UNO listener; semantic review also found broad process termination, unbounded archive extraction, unescaped XML insertion, and unpinned package installation.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting workflow terminates every soffice.bin process.
remediation.suggestion: Track the automation process ID and stop only that process after confirming no unsaved presentation work will be lost.

remediation.issue: Template archives are extracted without entry validation or resource limits.
remediation.suggestion: Validate archive paths and expanded size, reject links, cap resource use, and fail when extraction returns an error.

remediation.issue: Template values are inserted into content.xml without XML escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured XML library and insert values as escaped text nodes before rebuilding the ODP archive.

remediation.issue: The UNO listener accepts local socket connections without authentication.
remediation.suggestion: Use an isolated LibreOffice profile, start the listener only when required, and stop it immediately after automation.

remediation.issue: Python package installation examples do not pin versions or verify artifacts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed versions, use a trusted package index, and verify hashes in reproducible environments.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Process Termination Can Cause Data Loss
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting command terminates every soffice.bin process, including unrelated sessions with unsaved presentations, without confirmation or process scoping.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented killall command explicitly targets every process with the matching name, so unrelated LibreOffice sessions can be terminated.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Template Archive Extraction
semantic_findings.description: The template workflow extracts a supplied archive without checking entries, links, expanded size, or resource limits, enabling disk exhaustion or unsafe archive contents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template path is accepted directly and passed to unzip without validation or extraction limits.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped XML Template Injection
semantic_findings.description: Placeholder values are inserted directly into content.xml, allowing supplied text to break XML structure or inject unintended ODF markup.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example performs direct string replacement with str(value) and does not use XML parsing or escaping.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Python Package Installation
semantic_findings.description: The installation examples fetch latest package versions without pins or hashes, increasing dependency drift and package supply-chain exposure.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both pip commands omit versions and integrity hashes, so installation results can change without review.

content.value_statement: Manual presentation creation and format conversion are repetitive and difficult to standardize. This skill provides LibreOffice Impress workflows for creation, templating, automation, and conversion.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of ODP presentations through LibreOffice commands and Python UNO.
Shows conversion workflows between ODP, PPTX, and PDF formats.
Demonstrates batch conversion of multiple ODP files to PDF.
Provides a Python example for populating and rebuilding an ODP template.
Explains local UNO socket setup for automated presentation workflows.
limitations: LibreOffice must be installed, and Python workflows may require additional packages.
Examples require adaptation, permission checks, and validation before production use.
The template example does not escape XML values or validate untrusted archives.
Conversion fidelity varies for fonts, charts, animations, and unsupported format features.

use_cases.title: Convert Client Presentations
use_cases.description: Convert ODP and PPTX files into delivery formats while preserving editable source files.

use_cases.title: Automate Recurring Reports
use_cases.description: Populate a standard presentation template with updated business data for each reporting cycle.

use_cases.title: Build Presentation Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use headless LibreOffice and UNO to create, convert, and validate presentations in automated workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Presentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert the ODP file at [path] to PDF. Preserve the source and report the output path and conversion errors.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion of a single local file

prompt_templates.title: Batch Convert a Folder
prompt_templates.prompt: Batch convert every ODP file in [folder] to PDF. Quote paths, avoid overwriting files, and summarize failures.

prompt_templates.title: Populate an ODP Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ODP presentation from [template] using [placeholder values]. Escape XML content and validate the generated presentation.

prompt_templates.title: Design a UNO Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python UNO workflow using [data source] and [layout rules]. Export PPTX and PDF, then validate both outputs.

output_examples.input: Convert quarterly-review.odp to PDF for distribution.
output_examples.output: A PDF copy is produced from the ODP source, followed by a conversion validation note.

output_examples.input: Generate a client deck from an ODP template and supplied section values.
output: A populated ODP presentation based on the supplied template.
A review note covering XML safety, layout fidelity, and output validation.

best_practices: Work on copies and keep ODP source files under version control.
Quote paths, validate formats, and check every command result before continuing.
Use slide masters and test exports in every required target format.
anti_patterns: Do not run killall for troubleshooting; stop only the LibreOffice process started for automation.
Do not insert untrusted values into ODP XML through direct string replacement.
Do not assume conversions preserve fonts, animations, charts, or layout without review.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: LibreOffice is required. Python UNO, ezodf, or odfpy may be needed for specific automation workflows.

faq.question: Which presentation formats are covered?
faq.answer: Guidance covers ODP, PPTX, PDF, HTML, and SWF, but installed LibreOffice filters determine actual support.

faq.question: Can the skill edit existing presentations?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines UNO automation and ODP template manipulation, but complex edits require additional implementation.

faq.question: Can conversions run without the desktop interface?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented soffice commands support headless conversion and batch processing.

faq.question: Is the template workflow safe for untrusted files?
faq.answer: No. Validate archive entries and sizes, escape XML values, and isolate processing before handling untrusted templates.

faq.question: Will converted presentations look identical?
faq.answer: Not always. Fonts, animations, charts, and unsupported features can change, so review every target format.
